style: Say in a relaxed, friendly way, like a kind dad helping with homework
lines: Pick a problem on the street. Then tap the neighbors to hear what they think.
You've heard enough to start. Tap Make the play, or keep listening.
Tap Add character. Pick two or three neighbors for your play.
Now choose who or what is in their way. That's where the drama comes from.
Pick a backdrop, wings and props. Then dress your puppets.
Write three short scenes. Pick a speaker, then a line, or type your own.
The stage check found a problem. Read the cross, then fix it.
Nobody is in anybody's way, so nothing happens. Tap Characters and give someone a blocker.
All three checks pass. Tap Perform when you're ready.
Pick your role, then tap Curtain. Tap Next line after each line.
That's your line. Read it out loud, then tap Next line.
Take a bow. What does your play say about this street?
Tap Add character to choose one more neighbor. A play needs at least two characters.
Choose What do they try, then tick who the fix helps. You can edit any line in the script.
Read the speech bubble aloud. Tap Next line, or press Space, to continue.
Tap Bow to finish your play. Then write what it says about this neighborhood.
Write your closing answer. Tap From the top to perform your play again.
Tap another neighbor on the street. Hear at least three, then tap Make the play.
Pick a speaker and a suggested line, or type your own. Tap Add line to put it in this scene.
Choose a speaker and line, or type your own. Tap Save line to replace this line.
This scene has six lines. Tap Edit on a script line to change it, or remove a line to make room.
